mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, market expectations for future rate hikes diminish, lowering discount rates and thereby increasing the present value of equities, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS is below its 2-year rolling average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 60-day mean during similar low-rate regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which raises risk premia and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: During similar labor-market transition events, 20-day forward returns are not significantly more negative than during baseline periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a sustained decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates strengthening supply capacity without price pressure, lowering growth risk and supporting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >5% month-over-month while CPIAUCSL falls by >0.5% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In analogous supply-side expansion episodes, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in residential construction (HOUST) coupled with elevated consumer demand (GDPC1) suggests a structural supply shock that outpaces demand, raising growth uncertainty and depressing equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >10% for 3 consecutive months while GDPC1 rises by >4% month-over-month
failure_condition: During comparable supply-constrained episodes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly more negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds +2% in a month, it indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise rates, which compresses discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: During inflation spikes with similar magnitude, 60-day forward returns are not significantly more negative than during baseline inflation periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in labor force participation (PAYEMS) without a corresponding drop in unemployment (UNRATE) suggests demographic or structural discouragement, lowering economic growth prospects and increasing risk aversion, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by >2% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months while UNRATE remains flat or rises slightly
regime_hint: Labor force decline without job market softening
failure_condition: In comparable labor force contraction episodes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly more negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies; use proxy GDPC1 as a demand proxy) coinciding with a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates shifting consumer versus business demand, raising uncertainty and depressing equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >8% in a month while INDPRO falls by >6% in the same month
failure_condition: During analogous demand-supply decoupling events, 5-day forward returns are not significantly more negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) while industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat suggests a supply-side soft landing, lowering growth expectations and reducing equity risk premia, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >1% for 2 consecutive months while INDPRO is flat for the same period
failure_condition: In similar soft landing episodes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly more positive than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
